A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:

rejected.title: Parts of an animal cell
card: Nucleus
The control centre of the cell. It holds the genetic material, which has the instructions for how the cell works.
Cell membrane
A thin layer around the cell. It controls what goes in and out, so it lets useful things in and wastes out.
Cytoplasm
A jelly-like fluid that fills the cell. Most of the cell's chemical reactions happen here.
Each part has its own job, and the cell works because the parts do their jobs together.
rejected.remember: Nucleus controls and stores instructions, membrane controls entry and exit, cytoplasm is where reactions happen.

a.q: A scientist removes the nucleus from an animal cell. Which job can the cell no longer be directed to do?
opts: Follow its genetic instructions to work properly
Keep its contents inside a thin outer layer
Hold the jelly-like fluid that fills the cell
Let wastes pass out of the cell
a.why: The nucleus holds the genetic material, which has the instructions that control the cell. The membrane and cytoplasm are separate parts, so the outer layer, the fluid and the movement of wastes are not the nucleus's jobs.
a.clue: Which part is the control centre?

b.q: A chemical harms the cell membrane of an animal cell, so it can no longer control what enters. What is the most likely problem for the cell?
opts: Harmful substances get in and useful ones leak out
The nucleus stops storing the genetic material
The cytoplasm stops being where reactions happen
Nothing changes, as the nucleus controls what enters
b.why: The cell membrane is the part that controls what goes in and out, so damage to it lets the wrong things pass. It is tempting to think the nucleus controls entry because it is the control centre, but that job belongs to the membrane. The nucleus still holds the genetic material and the cytoplasm is still where reactions happen.
b.clue: Which part acts as the gatekeeper of the cell?

b.q: A chemical harms the cell membrane of an animal cell, so it can no longer control what enters. What is the most likely problem for the cell?
opts: Harmful substances may enter and useful ones may leave
The genetic material can no longer be stored

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ('may'). The distractors are all absolute ('at once', 'can no longer'), so a student could pick it without knowing what the membrane does.
